title: French Essentials (KS3 French)
subject: French
strapline: Core verbs, phrases and grammar to get talking.
facts: Greetings: bonjour (hello), salut (hi/bye), au revoir (goodbye), s’il vous plaît (please), merci (thank you).
French nouns have a gender: masculine (le) or feminine (la); plural is les.
The verb être (to be): je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont.
The verb avoir (to have): j’ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont.
To say your age you use avoir: "j’ai treize ans" literally means "I have thirteen years".
Adjectives usually go after the noun and agree in gender and number: un chat noir, une voiture noire.
Common question words: qui (who), que (what), où (where), quand (when), pourquoi (why), comment (how).

quick_quiz.q: How do you say "thank you" in French?
Which verb do the French use to give their age?

teacher_tips: Drill être and avoir early — they unlock most beginner sentences.
Teach gender with the article, never the noun alone.
Use lots of spoken repetition before written work.
